verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 1 — Repair the KP14 truth: regenerate integ_results.npz and G_func.csv, fix the H/L regime convention
verdicts.critique:
MANDATORY, and I verified the core claim myself rather than taking it on faith. `utils_kp14/KP14_solfiles/integ_results.npz` returns EXACTLY 0.0 for E_t[G_up], E_t[G_down], E_t[A_mod] and all eight companion integrals on a contiguous eps block spanning roughly [0.80, 1.044] — precisely the region the simulated panel occupies (eps ~ 1.000 +/- 0.024). The first nonzero grid point above the panel's support is eps = 1.049. Independent scale check: with current config.py parameters the steady-state growth-option value is C*A_mod(1)/KP14_RHO = 68,818, while G_func.csv reports G_up(1) = 1,622; recomputing with the pre-Jun-18 gamma_x = 1.38 gives 1,142, i.e. the shipped file is a solve under the OLD parameters, off by ~42x. So `term2` in panel_functions_kp14.py:193 contributes ~1% of the PVGO continuation value it should, and every KP14 number in the paper — rp, cond_var, max_sr, sdf_ret, the 'true SDF weights' in correlations.csv, the -2.64/-5.35 Sharpes — is a quadrature artifact. As a referee I cannot evaluate the KP14 column of any table until this is fixed, and the paper must DISCLOSE that previously circulated KP14 results were void. That disclosure is survivable; burying it is not.

THREE THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THE PROPOSAL AS WRITTEN.
(i) FACTUAL ERROR ON THE REGIME FIX. The proposal asserts 'kp14_fd.py:100-101 weights G2 consistently with P(high)=0.3191'. It does not. I read the file: `G_out[:,0] = G[:,0] + mu_L/(mu_L+mu_H)*(lambda_H-lambda_L)*G[:,1]`, i.e. weight 0.6809 — the SIMULATION's convention, contradicting the proposal's own diagnosis text. So the code splits 2-to-1 in favor of P(H)=0.6809 (panel_functions_kp14.py:98 and kp14_fd.py:100-101) against one line (config.py:257). The proposal's fix (c)/(d) flips the two majority sites and leaves kp14_fd.py inconsistent.
(ii) THE ARGUMENT FOR THE FIX IS NOT AN ARGUMENT. 'LAMBDA_L would be negative under w=0.6809, therefore 0.3191 is intended' is equally an argument that LAMBDA_H = 2.35 is too large to be the majority state. Under the standard continuous-time two-state convention mu_H is the exit rate FROM H, so line 98 is the conventional reading and config.py:257 is the typo. Choosing the resolution that changes which regime is the majority state — and hence the whole firm-size and growth-option distribution — rather than the one that rescales a normalization constant is exactly the discretionary choice a referee flags. Resolve it against KP14's published calibration, not against internal consistency, and say in the text which you did and why.
(iii) QUOTED DIAGNOSTICS DON'T REPLICATE. The proposal reports 322/1000 nonzeros in A_mod_lst; I measure 762/1000. The zero region still covers the panel support so the substance holds, but the mismatch suggests the diagnosis was run against a different file than the one in the repo. Re-run and re-quote before anything goes in a footnote.

ATTRIBUTION: 100% plumbing. That is the right call here — it buys correctness, not a result — and the proposal is commendably explicit that it will NOT create a DKKM gap.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It will not, and the proposal says so. After repair, PVGO/P rises to roughly 0.5-0.6 and beta_z = alph*share becomes a live second factor — but I confirm the proposer's own killer observation: price = VAP + PVGO is homogeneous of degree one in x (panel_functions_kp14.py:165, 173), so beta_x = 1 for EVERY firm, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 hard-codes that by factoring Et_x2[t] out of the entire cross-firm block. With one uniform-loading factor and one factor whose loading is affine in book-to-market, FM's span (fama_functions.py:158-160, P = X pinv(X'X) on [1, chars]) contains the whole thing exactly. Expect FF ~ FM ~ DKKM at Sharpe ~0.15-0.22/month. A second worry the proposal understates: KP14_RHO = 0.0158/yr, so the growth-option Feynman-Kac operator sits 1.6 percentage points from the transversality boundary (rho = 0 at gamma_z = -0.4294, which I verified). PVGO ~ 1/rho means the repaired model's central object is governed by a near-singular denominator; a referee will ask how a 20% change in gamma_z can change firm value by a factor of 5, and the honest answer is that the calibration is on a knife-edge.
verdicts.salvage: Do (a) and (b) — the quadrature fix and the parameters_kp14.py shim — unconditionally; they are the paper's precondition. Replace (c)/(d) with: keep the simulation as coded (P(H) = 0.6809, the conventional CTMC reading and the reading kp14_fd.py already uses) and instead fix config.py:257 to LAMBDA_L = (1 - P_H*LAMBDA_H)/(1 - P_H) with P_H = MU_L/(MU_H+MU_L), lowering LAMBDA_H until LAMBDA_L is positive — a normalization change, not an economic one. Do (e). Add: propagate `max_sr` (computed at sdf_compute_kp14.py:294-296, saved into moments, then silently dropped — grep evaluate_sdfs.py, it never appears) into results.pkl and report every Sharpe as Sharpe/SR*, the Sigma-metric cosine. Without that number a referee cannot tell whether DKKM/FF = 1.04 is 1.04x of 5% of the ceiling or of 90%, and the table is uninterpretable regardless of which model change you adopt. Finally, add a transversality diagnostic to the paper: report rho and the distance to rho = 0.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 2 — Investment-specific technology SPACE: K priced technology-domain shocks over an observable 2-D technology map
verdicts.critique:
This is the only proposal that attacks the binding constraint identified by every diagnosis agent — the priced-risk space is one- or two-dimensional — and its algebra is sound. I verified the two arithmetic claims that matter: d(rho)/d(gamma_z) = alph*sigma_z = 0.1983 so rho = 0 at g = -0.4294 exactly as stated, and the generalized moment E_t[z_i'^a z_j'^a] = Et_z_alph_i * Et_z_alph_j * exp(a^2 rho_ij sigma_z^2 dt) does reduce to the existing Et_z_alph2 (sdf_compute_kp14.py:107) at rho_ij = 1. The sdf_compute changes really are six lines and really do stay O(N^2). Credit where due.

BUT AS PARAMETERIZED THIS IS UNPUBLISHABLE, AND FOR FIVE SEPARATE REASONS.
(1) THE TARGET IS REVERSE-ENGINEERED, IN WRITING. The proposal computes SR* = 3.118/yr and then says 'This lands exactly on DKKM's real-data attainable Sharpe of 3.7.' That sentence, or any sentence like it, appearing anywhere near this calibration is fatal. K, GAMMA_Z_BAR and SIGMA_GAMMA_Z have no external discipline — K = 100 is chosen because 'the gap scales as sqrt(m_DKKM/m_FM) and needs K >> L', i.e. it is chosen to make the estimator comparison come out. That is the definition of changing the model until you get the answer you want.
(2) THE PRICES OF RISK HAVE RANDOM SIGNS. GAMMA_Z_BAR*q = -0.175 with SIGMA_GAMMA_Z = 0.30 means the cross-domain sd of the IST price of risk is 1.7x its mean, so ~28% of technology domains have a POSITIVE IST premium. The proposal frames this as creative destruction. But nothing in the model distinguishes a creative-destruction domain from a cost-reduction domain — gamma_k is an i.i.d. normal label attached to a uniformly-random torus coordinate. Economically these are 100 unnamed priced factors with random signs, not technology domains.
(3) EXISTENCE DEPENDS ON A HARD TRUNCATION. At alpha = 0.75, rho(g) = 0.111025 + 0.105*g. The 2.5-sigma truncation gives worst-case g = -0.925, rho = 0.0139 > 0. At 3 sigma, g = -1.075 and rho = -0.0019 < 0: no equilibrium, infinite growth-option value. With K = 100 domains, an untruncated draw exceeds 3 sigma with probability ~12% per simulation. The clip() is load-bearing for the existence of the model, and a referee who notices will not be persuaded by 'we truncated at 2.5 sd.'
(4) IT REQUIRES A COINCIDENT ESTIMATOR CHANGE, AND THE PROPOSAL ADMITS THE MODEL CHANGE ALONE BUYS 1.13x. Rescaling GAMMA_GRID (config.py:211) by 4.31 is defensible on DKKM's own terms, but it is a DKKM-only tuning knob applied in the same revision as the model change that makes it pay. Worse, the proposal misses that the rescale is partly a no-op: dkkm_functions.py:110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a SECOND time, and rank-standardization is invariant to monotone transforms, so gamma barely moves the realized feature matrix until sin actually folds. You must fix line 110 in the same breath or the 2.19x will not materialize and you will have burned the disclosure cost for nothing.
(5) THE ADDED CHARACTERISTICS BREAK FF AND ARE NOT INFORMATION-NEUTRAL. fama_functions.py:61-62 hardcodes _CHAR_TO_FACTOR and `factor_dct[name_dct[char]]` at line 104 raises KeyError on tech1/tech2 — the proposal catches this. What it does not catch: handing FF two new characteristics means two more value-weighted 2x3 size-crossed tercile sorts, which is nearly useless for recovering a smooth function on a torus, while handing DKKM the same two characteristics raises sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) and enriches its kernel. 'Same information set' is satisfied in letter and violated in spirit.

ATTRIBUTION: roughly 50/50 economics/plumbing at the coded bandwidth (1.13x is within noise of nothing), tipping to majority-plumbing once the 2.19x figure is quoted, because half of that comes from GAMMA_GRID.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, but less than claimed, and the honest linear benchmark closes much of it. The true weight's priced part is share_i * g_t(theta_i)/d_i with g_t a smooth function on the torus. FM as coded cannot form share*g(theta) — correct. But the referee's demand is immediate and obvious: rerun FM on [1, chars, theta1, theta2, theta1^2, theta2^2, theta1*theta2, bm*theta1, bm*theta2] — nine extra columns, still OLS, still T=360, K=16 << 360, so essentially no estimation cost (plug-in loss ~2K/T = 9%). That augmented-linear benchmark captures every quadratic mode of g, which is exactly the set of modes DKKM reaches at the CODED bandwidth. The 1.13x evaporates entirely. The 2.19x survives only because the rescaled RFF reaches ~45 modes — so what is actually being measured is 'a 45-mode basis beats a 6-mode basis at recovering a function with 100 modes', which is dimension counting, not the virtue of complexity. The diagnosis phase already ran the controlling placebo in GS21: 150 RANDOM Gaussian directions carrying zero characteristic information attained 0.74-0.82 of max SR^2. Any referee who knows that number will demand the same placebo here, and a large share of the DKKM advantage will show up in it.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the mechanism, kill the calibration. (a) Set K to something economically nameable — 10 to 12 domains matched to BEA equipment-price categories or 2-digit SIC, with gamma_k CALIBRATED to observed cross-category equipment-price trends rather than drawn i.i.d. normal, and with all gamma_k the same SIGN so the economics ('IST progress is bad news for growth-option holders') survives. Accept that this yields ~1.1-1.2x, and report it as such. (b) Make theta a function of something the firm already has — e.g. assign domains by the vintage of the firm's oldest live project, or by lambda_f decile — rather than an exogenous uniform label, so a referee cannot say you planted two noise coordinates that only the nonlinear estimator can read. (c) Move alpha to 0.75 REGARDLESS of whether you adopt the rest: the current KP14_RHO = 0.0158 knife-edge is a defect in the baseline and this is a clean, independently defensible fix. (d) Run the D2 population-span diagnostic (max_a SR over the RFF span vs the linear-char span, using true rp and cond_var from the moments pickle, zero estimation error) BEFORE writing any of the code. If the oracle ratio is below 2, do not build it.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 3 — Historical-cost book value plus vintage/count/investment-intensity/cash-flow-volatility characteristics
verdicts.critique:
This is the most defensible change in the set and the one I would let through with the least argument. Marking book to current replacement cost (panel_functions_kp14.py:144, `book = x/z*K.sum(axis=0)`) is a modelling convenience, not an accounting fact; the historical-cost version is literally the sum of the cash outflows the model already records at line 157 (`-K*x/z` at installation). Recording what the firm paid is not a tuning choice, it is a correction, and it can be defended in one sentence to any referee. The four added characteristics (capital age, project count, trailing investment intensity, trailing cash-flow volatility) are all standard, all observable, all already latent in the state. Cost is genuinely zero to sdf_compute: I confirmed `keep = book[t,:] > 0` (sdf_compute_kp14.py:269) still means 'at least one live project' under historical cost, since x/z > 0 always.

THREE PROBLEMS.
(i) IT WILL NOT PRODUCE A RESULT, AND THE PROPOSAL SAYS SO (+2% to +5%). A referee reading a paper whose headline is 'complexity pays' will not accept a 1.03x as evidence of anything.
(ii) THE L=5 vs L=9 CONFOUND IS REAL AND THE PROPOSAL'S OWN MITIGATION IS INSUFFICIENT. Going from 5 to 9 characteristics raises sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) from 0.645 to 0.866 at gamma = 1, which materially enriches the DKKM kernel, while it hands FF four more degenerate tercile sorts. Running L=5 and L=9 as separate arms (the proposal's suggestion) shows the confound exists; it does not remove it. The clean design is a third arm: L=9 with GAMMA_GRID rescaled so sd(Wx) is held at its L=5 value, isolating the pure information effect.
(iii) agr DEGENERACY PROPAGATES. `agr` is built at panel_functions_kp14.py:262-267 from pct_change of a lumpy, Poisson-driven book. In BGN the identical construction yields q30 == q70 == 0 and an FF 'cma' sort that is a 92/8 split with an EMPTY medium leg (fama_functions.py:82-84). invint = rolling(60).sum(agr) inherits that lumpiness. If cma and invint both degenerate, FF is handicapped by a coding artifact rather than by economics, and the DKKM-over-FF gap you report is partly a broken benchmark. Assert q30 != q70 for every char in every eval month before reporting a table.

ATTRIBUTION: ~70% economics, 30% plumbing (the L=5/L=9 bandwidth side effect is plumbing and must be netted out).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No — and this is the proposal that dies most cleanly to the robustness check I would demand. Its entire mechanism is one bilinear term: beta_z,i = alph*(1 - bm_i * exp(c0 + c1*age_i)), i.e. bm x a smooth function of age. Add {bm*age, bm*age^2, age^2} to the FM design matrix — three columns, still OLS, still trivially estimable at T=360 — and FM captures it. The proposer even concedes DKKM reaches it only because 86.7% of the coded RFF feature variance lies in the 21-dim QUADRATIC span of the chars; anything reachable by a quadratic is reachable by an augmented linear regression. More damaging: the proposal's own risk section notes the historical-cost wedge is driven by (x_t/z_t) relative to installation-date values, which is a function of AGGREGATE history — so across firms it varies only through the vintage MIX, and the proposal's own arithmetic shows the firm-level wedge sd is 0.174 in logs and is FLAT in delta (halving delta leaves it at 0.174). A 17% multiplicative wedge on the bm-to-share mapping is not a source of high-dimensional nonlinearity; it is a small amount of measurement noise in bm, which degrades every method roughly equally.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt the historical-cost change on correctness grounds and say exactly that in the paper — 'we correct book equity to historical cost; this changes results negligibly' is a strengthening sentence, not a weakening one. Adopt cfvol specifically, because it is the one addition with a distinct role: it makes 1/d_i directly learnable rather than only through size, which is the precondition for the heteroskedastic-D multiplier that Proposals 2 and 6 need. Drop the framing that this proposal contributes to the headline result. Replace 'run L=5 and L=9 as separate arms' with the bandwidth-held-fixed third arm. And pre-commit to reporting FM-with-interactions as the benchmark, because if you do not, the referee will, and then the number appears in the report rather than the paper.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 4 — Firm-level, non-diversifying productivity risk: recalibrate theta_eps/sigma_eps and project count
verdicts.critique:
The diagnosis this rests on is right: after the Jun-18 cut (config.py:247-250, KP14_SIGMA_EPS = 0.1*0.2, KP14_SIGMA_U = 0.1*1.5) the CIR shocks supply ~2% of idiosyncratic variance and the rest is Poisson project-count lumpiness, which makes d_i ~ 1/n_live ~ 1/size mechanically and drives the documented negative Sharpes. Fixing that is worth doing. And the proposal is admirably honest that standalone it moves DKKM/FM from 1.00 to 1.02.

BUT THE OPTICS ARE THE WORST OF ANY PROPOSAL HERE. You are proposing to move FOUR deep structural parameters at once — theta_eps down 3.5x, sigma_eps up 9x, sigma_u up 3x, mu_lambda and sigma_lambda up 4x — each justified by a different empirical literature (Syverson for TFP dispersion, Foster-Haltiwanger-Syverson for persistence, nothing at all for mu_lambda = sigma_lambda = 8), all in the direction that helps, in a revision whose stated purpose is to make DKKM win. The two sigma changes explicitly REVERSE a cut the authors themselves made two months earlier. A referee will read the git log. 'We reverted our own 10x parameter cut and quadrupled firm size because it improved the estimator comparison' is not a sentence that survives review, and there is no way to phrase it that does.

A TECHNICAL PROBLEM THE PROPOSAL MISSES. A(eps,u) = A_0 + (eps-1)A_1 + (u-1)A_2 + (eps-1)(u-1)A_3 is a first-order approximation around eps = u = 1, and project capital is K_j = (alpha*z*A(eps,1))^(1/(1-alpha)) with exponent 6.667 at alpha = 0.85. With A_0 = 4.354 and A_1 = 1.725 (which the proposal raises to 3.033 by cutting theta_eps), pushing sd(eps) from 0.024 to 0.402 means a 2-sd-low eps gives A = 2.97 and K = (2.97/4.354)^6.667 = 0.055 of baseline — an 18x size difference from a single shock, through a linear approximation evaluated 2.5 standard deviations outside its point of expansion. The proposal checks only that A stays positive. That is not enough: the whole size distribution, and hence the size/idio-variance relation this proposal is trying to break, becomes an artifact of extrapolating a Taylor expansion.

ATTRIBUTION: 100% plumbing in the sense that matters — it changes no economic mechanism, only the magnitude of an existing one, and by the proposal's own estimate changes the headline ratio by 2%.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal concedes it. The claimed value is entirely as a multiplier on Proposal 2 or 6. But the multiplier argument itself is weaker than presented. The span experiment quoted (RFF/linear ceiling 1.00 -> 1.91 when heteroskedastic D is added to a linear alpha) used d ~ exp(6*x2), i.e. sd(log d) = 1.73 and a 20x variance spread driven by a SINGLE clean characteristic. This proposal delivers sd(log d) somewhere near 0.7-1.0 with log d already 88% LINEARLY predictable from the raw chars (measured R^2 = 0.880). When log d is linear in x, FM's shortfall is only the curvature of exp(-b'x), which at sd(log d) = 1.0 is ~13% of the variance of 1/d — and a referee will simply ask you to add exp of the fitted linear index, or a squared term, to the FM design. Separately: the proposal's headline extension (heterogeneous sigma_eps,i on a 7-point grid, reported as cfvol) is the part that would actually break the size link, and it requires solving G and eleven integrals on a 7-node sigma grid on top of Proposal 2's 20-node rho grid — 140 solves. That is real machinery introduced to move a ratio by 2%.
verdicts.salvage: Split it. (a) Adopt a MINIMAL version framed purely as a bug correction rather than a recalibration: the current calibration makes 98% of firm risk 'did a plant close', which is indefensible on its face, so restore sigma_eps and sigma_u to their pre-Jun-18 values (i.e. delete the two `0.1*` factors at config.py:248 and 250) and STOP. One change, one sentence, no new literature citations, and it demonstrably improves the conditioning of cond_var (680 -> 165). (b) Leave theta_eps, mu_lambda and sigma_lambda alone; there is no defensible story for quadrupling firm size other than that it helps. (c) If you want d_i to stop tracking size, do it the honest way: make sigma_eps,i firm-specific and INDEPENDENT of lambda_f, disclose it as a deliberate device, and report the resulting corr(log d, log size) as a calibration target against the real-data value of roughly -0.35. That is a defensible modelling choice; recalibrating four parameters is not. (d) Before any of this, verify A(eps,u) > 0 and check the implied sd(log K) against real sd(log market cap) ~ 2.0.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 5 — Heterogeneous operating leverage: a firm-specific fixed operating cost per project
verdicts.critique:
The best economics-per-line in the set, and the only proposal attacking the single most embarrassing structural fact about KP14 as implemented, which I verified directly: VAP = x*K^alpha*A(eps,u) (panel_functions_kp14.py:165) and PVGO = z^alph*x*lambda_f*G(eps) (line 173) are both homogeneous of degree one in x, so beta_x = 1 for EVERY firm, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 bakes that in by factoring Et_x2[t] out of the whole cross-firm block. The dominant price of risk (gamma_x = 0.69) therefore generates literally zero cross-sectional dispersion in exposure. Any referee shown that fact will regard the KP14 cross-section as vacuous. Operating leverage is the canonical, heavily-cited fix (Carlson-Fisher-Giammarino, Zhang, Novy-Marx), it is disclosed in one sentence, and nobody will accuse you of inventing it to win an estimator horse race. That is the highest bar any of these proposals clears.

FOUR CONCERNS.
(i) THIS IS THE RISKIEST CODE SURGERY IN THE SET, AND THE PROPOSAL UNDERSTATES IT. sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 is a single line that carries the entire O(N^2) cross-firm block and is valid ONLY under x-homogeneity. Splitting P' into an x-proportional and an x-independent piece requires new closed forms for E[n' Q'] and E[n'^2] and a rewrite of the term4 cash-flow correction at lines 162-165, whose `- np.outer(cf/price, cf/price)` double-counting subtraction is only correct under the current normalization. There are two commented-out single-pair validation blocks in the file (lines 148-159 and 231-254) that must be un-commented and made to pass. If they do not, every number in the KP14 column is silently wrong in a way no assertion will catch — which is precisely how the integ_results.npz failure survived.
(ii) THE LEVEL EFFECT CONTAMINATES THE MARKET PREMIUM. mean beta_x = 1.207 raises the equity premium from 8.97% to 10.8%/yr. The proposal's own fix (rescale gamma_x to 0.572) triggers a re-solve because gamma_x enters KP14_CONST and hence A_0..A_3 and KP14_RHO (config.py:264-272). Do it anyway: leaving the market premium free to move with the operating-leverage calibration lets a referee argue you tuned the aggregate premium.
(iii) NEGATIVE EQUITY. The proposal caps kappa at 0.60 to keep projects NPV-positive, but a high-kappa firm in a bad eps state can still have P <= 0, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:269 filters only on book > 0. Extend the keep mask to price > 0 and report the frequency.
(iv) TWO MORE CHARACTERISTICS, SAME FF PROBLEM. grossmargin and salesprice must be added to config.py:229-236 AND both hardcoded copies of _CHAR_TO_FACTOR (fama_functions.py:61-62 and 170-171) or fama_french KeyErrors at line 104. And note grossmargin = 1 - kappa is a CONSTANT for each firm forever — a fixed firm label, which after rank-standardization is a perfectly persistent characteristic. That is fine economically but it means the DKKM kernel gets a free, noiseless firm fixed effect, which is worth flagging.

ATTRIBUTION: ~85% economics, 15% plumbing. The highest economics share of any proposal here.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Only if the referee lets you keep FM linear, and the referee will not. The mechanism is exactly beta_x,i = 1 + kappa_i*(Rev_i/P_i)/(r+delta) — a single product of two observable characteristics. The proposal is candid that this works at the CODED bandwidth precisely because 86.7% of the RFF feature variance is quadratic in the chars. But anything a quadratic reaches, a quadratic-augmented OLS reaches better: add kappa*salesprice (one column) to fama_macbeth's design at fama_functions.py:158-160 and FM captures the entire mechanism with 8 parameters and T = 360, i.e. at essentially zero estimation cost, while DKKM pays P/T = 10 complexity risk to reach the same function. My prediction is that augmented-FM BEATS DKKM under this proposal, not ties it. There is a second, subtler problem: the two ingredients are not independent. Rev/P is itself close to (1 - PVGO share)/A_0, which is close to affine in bm — so kappa*(Rev/P) is close to kappa*bm, one interaction among two chars, in a 7-char space. That is a 1-dimensional nonlinearity, and one-dimensional nonlinearities are what small models are for. Finally, FF should IMPROVE here (a gross-margin 2x3 sort is a real factor), which narrows the DKKM-over-FF gap that is the paper's headline comparison.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt it, but adopt it as a MODEL CORRECTION rather than as the source of the result, and lead with that framing: 'the implementation had beta_x = 1 for every firm; we add heterogeneous operating leverage so that the dominant priced shock has a nontrivial cross-section.' That sentence is unimpeachable. Then report, in the same table, FM augmented with the interaction, and accept that the DKKM gap is small. Two amplifications worth trying since they cost nothing extra: (a) make kappa_i time-varying and mean-reverting rather than a permanent firm label, so it is a genuine characteristic rather than a fixed effect and so FF's static sort is not artificially handicapped; (b) let the fixed cost be denominated in a factor whose price differs from x (e.g. a wage that co-moves with the aggregate state), which turns beta_x,i into a ratio of two aggregate exposures rather than an affine function of one — that is a genuinely non-quadratic object and is the version augmented-FM cannot absorb. Combine with Proposal 1 (mandatory) and, if you take anything from Proposal 4, only the sigma_eps restoration.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 6 — Persistent mean-reverting demand wedge on price with a fundamental anchor nonlinear in the characteristics
verdicts.critique:
This is the proposal that would kill the paper, and it would kill it in one sentence in my report: THE AUTHORS ASSUME AN EXPECTED-RETURN COMPONENT THAT IS A NONLINEAR FUNCTION OF CHARACTERISTICS AND THEN REPORT, AS A FINDING, THAT A NONLINEAR ESTIMATOR RECOVERS IT BETTER THAN A LINEAR ONE.

The proposal knows this — it lists 'IT CHANGES WHAT TRUE MEANS' as its first risk and calls itself the most contested choice in the set. That self-awareness does not save it, for three reasons.
(1) THE PAPER'S ENTIRE PREMISE IS THAT THESE ARE STRUCTURAL, FRICTIONLESS MODELS AND THE TRUTH IS THE MODEL'S OWN SDF. The title is 'The Virtue of Complexity in Simple ECONOMIC Models.' Bolting an exogenous OU noise process onto the price and declaring the resulting mispricing to be part of the true MVE is not a simple economic model producing the virtue of complexity; it is an assumption producing its own consequence. Reframing it as 'segmented markets' does not change the mathematics: w is an i.i.d.-across-firms exogenous process with no agent, no constraint and no market-clearing condition behind it.
(2) THE MAGNITUDE IS BACKED OUT FROM THE TARGET, EXPLICITLY. The derivation section is titled 'TARGET THE NEAR-ARBITRAGE SHARPE FIRST, THEN BACK OUT THE PARAMETERS' and proceeds from DKKM's real-data 3.7 to sd(alpha) to kappa_w*SD_W. Every parameter in the proposal is the solution to 'what makes the answer come out.' There is no independent moment being matched.
(3) THE RESULT WOULD BE A DIVERSIFICATION ARTIFACT. alpha'D^{-1}alpha ~ N*E[alpha^2/d] grows with N, so SR* = 1.36/month = 4.7/yr comes from 1000 quasi-independent bets with per-stock information ratio 0.034. That is a near-arbitrage in a model with no limits to arbitrage — the model contains a 4.7 Sharpe and no reason nobody takes it. A referee will ask why the demand wedge is not competed away by the very investor whose portfolio you are computing. The proposal's own N-robustness check (report N = 250/500/1000, show the RATIO is stable) is the right check but it does not answer the economic question, only the statistical one.

SEPARATELY, THE CODE SURGERY IS THE RISKIEST HERE AND THE PROPOSAL SAYS SO: unbundling term4 at sdf_compute_kp14.py:162-165 into a four-way expansion, where the existing `- np.outer(cf/price, cf/price)` is a double-counting correction valid only under the current normalization.

ATTRIBUTION: 0% economics in any sense a structural macro-finance referee would recognize. It is an assumption, and the resulting number measures how well each estimator inverts an assumed function.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Yes — it is the only proposal here that plausibly reaches 3-5x, which is exactly what makes it damning rather than persuasive. And even taking it on its own terms, the gap is not robust. alpha_i = kappa_w*dt*(log bm_i + h(chars_i)), so DKKM's advantage over FM is entirely 1 - R^2(h | linear chars). The proposal's own diagnostic instruction — 'if the linear R^2 is above 0.85, this proposal will not deliver' — concedes that the result is a free parameter set by how nonlinear you choose to make the fundamental-value map, and that map is itself made nonlinear only by adopting Proposals 3 and 5 first. So the chain is: assume a wedge, assume the anchor is nonlinear, then measure that a nonlinear estimator inverts it better. Moreover, the wedge is orthogonal to everything, which means the alpha is recoverable ONLY through the chars — there is no unlearnable component and no reason FM cannot be augmented. Give FM the same degree-3 polynomial basis in the chars (56 columns, T = 360, still estimable) and it will recover most of h; the remaining DKKM edge is then shrinkage efficiency at c = P/T, i.e. the KMZ estimation-variance channel, which is a statistics result and not an economics result.
verdicts.salvage: Very little, and I would advise against attempting it in this paper. If you must have an unspanned premium, do it with a MICROFOUNDED friction rather than an exogenous price wedge: (a) a participation or short-sale constraint that binds as a function of firm characteristics, so the shadow price is an equilibrium object with a first-order condition behind it; (b) heterogeneous investors with genuinely different SDFs and a market-clearing condition, so the observed price reflects a wealth-weighted average and the 'alpha' relative to any one agent's SDF is an equilibrium outcome rather than an assumption; (c) intermediary capital constraints. Each of those is a real paper's worth of work and none is a KP14 patch. The far better use of this insight is REPORTING it: state in the paper that the diagnosis establishes, with an explicit population-span computation, that under exact K-factor pricing with N = 1000 every basis attains the maximum Sharpe to within 0.2%, and therefore that NO frictionless production model can generate the virtue of complexity. That is a clean, novel, publishable negative result. It is also, in my view, the paper you actually have.

missed_ideas: FIX THE BENCHMARK BEFORE FIXING THE MODEL — this is the omission that matters most, and it is a fairness defect that will kill the paper regardless of which economic change you adopt. I verified it: config.py:187 sets ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0], so FF/FM get plain OLS with one specification and zero tuning decisions, while config.py:190 gives DKKM six alphas and config.py:181 four feature counts = 24 cells, and create_slides_tables.py:81-97 (find_best_alpha_for_model) then selects the argmax/argmin cell USING THE REPORTED EVALUATION METRIC ITSELF, pooled across all iterations. GS21 additionally gets a hand-tuned grid (ALPHA_LST_GS = ALPHA_LST/100, config.py:193, 333) — model-specific tuning applied to DKKM only. So the current headline 'DKKM ties FF/FM' is an oracle-tuned DKKM tying an untuned FF/FM, and any post-change 'DKKM beats FF/FM' inherits the same defect. Required: (a) give FF/FM a ridge grid of the same cardinality and select their alpha the same way, or (b) select DKKM's alpha and nfeatures INSIDE the 360-month training window by cross-validation, never on the evaluation metric. Report the full 6x4 grid in an appendix, not the argmax cell. No proposal mentions this.

REPORT max_sr AND THE SIGMA-METRIC COSINE. max_sr is computed at sdf_compute_kp14.py:294-296 and saved into the moments pickle, but evaluate_sdfs.py never propagates it (I grepped — the string does not appear in the file), so it never reaches a table. Because Sharpe_t(w) = SR*_t * cos_Sigma(w, w*_t) is an exact identity, the interpretable quantity is Sharpe/SR*. Without it a referee cannot distinguish 'the estimator is failing' from 'the model has nothing to estimate', which is the entire question the paper is asking. This is a two-line change and it should precede every proposal here.

RUN THE ORACLE SPAN DIAGNOSTIC AS A GATE, NOT AS A POST-MORTEM. For each candidate model change, compute max_a SR(S_t a) with S_t = the configured RFF basis versus S_t = [1, chars], using the TRUE rp and cond_var already sitting in *_moments.pkl and zero estimation error. Report mean(SR_rff)/mean(SR_lin). Real-data DKKM-over-FF6 is 3-5x; below ~2 the model cannot deliver and no estimator tuning will change it. This costs minutes and would have pre-emptively killed Proposals 3, 4 and 5 and correctly identified 2 and 6 as the only candidates. Pre-register the threshold.

THE AUGMENTED-LINEAR BENCHMARK IS THE ROBUSTNESS CHECK THAT DECIDES THIS PAPER, AND NO PROPOSAL PRE-EMPTS IT. Proposals 3 and 5 each turn on exactly one bilinear interaction (bm x age; kappa x salesprice). Add those interactions to fama_macbeth's design (fama_functions.py:158-160) and the mechanism is absorbed at negligible estimation cost. Every proposal should be scored against 'FM on [1, chars, all pairwise products]' — 28 columns at L=7, T=360, still OLS — not against FM on 7 linear columns. A DKKM advantage that survives THAT is a real result; one that does not is a statement about the arbitrariness of the linear benchmark.

KP14'S OWN PROJECT-PORTFOLIO STRUCTURE IS AN UNEXPLOITED, FULLY NATIVE SOURCE OF HIGH-DIMENSIONAL NONLINEARITY. A firm is a portfolio of projects with heterogeneous (K_j, u_j, vintage). Firm value is currently a LINEAR aggregator over that portfolio (VAP = sum_j x*K_j^alpha*A(eps,u_j), panel_functions_kp14.py:165), which is why five low-order moments of the portfolio recover almost everything. Make the aggregator nonlinear using KP14's own machinery — firm-level decreasing returns, a capacity or managerial-attention constraint, or a financing constraint whose shadow price depends on the whole project distribution — and the map from observable portfolio moments to value becomes genuinely nonlinear with many quasi-orthogonal directions, WITHOUT inventing a technology torus (Proposal 2) or a demand wedge (Proposal 6). This is strictly more defensible than either and nobody proposed it.

NMAT=5 MISLABELS THE COMPLEXITY AXIS AND MUST BE SET TO 1. estimate_sdf_dkkm.py:134-169 averages stock weights across five independent W draws (config.py:178, with the comment noting the root codebase used nmat = 1). Averaging M random-feature ridge fits converges to KERNEL ridge with the same explicit penalty, cancelling exactly the draw-specific high-frequency components that finite-width random features are supposed to supply. It mechanically flattens the Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve — which is the curve the paper is trying to produce. Any proposal whose payoff is 'a rising virtue-of-complexity curve' is fighting this line of code. Set NMAT = 1 and report the five draws as replications.

THE SECOND RANK-STANDARDIZATION MAKES GAMMA_GRID NEARLY A NO-OP, WHICH BREAKS PROPOSALS 2 AND 4's ESTIMATOR FIX. dkkm_functions.py:110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a second time, and rank-standardization is invariant to strictly monotone transformations; since sin is monotone over the realized range of Wx for ~76% of directions at the coded bandwidth, rank_standardize(sin(gamma*w'x)) is numerically the rank of w'x regardless of gamma. Proposals 2 and 4 both rely on rescaling GAMMA_GRID by sqrt(130/L) and neither mentions line 110. The rescale must be paired with replacing the second rank-standardization by unit-variance standardization, or it will be partly absorbed and the predicted 2.19x will not appear.

THE 25 TEST ASSETS HAVE NO POWER AND WILL NOT ACQUIRE ANY UNDER ANY OF THESE PROPOSALS. generate_25_portfolios.py:112-113 sorts on mve and bm quintiles only — two of the characteristics every method already spans linearly — and compute_pricing_errors.py then runs each method's MVE return as a single factor against them. The paper's second headline claim (lower pricing error) is therefore untestable. Add test assets sorted on the specific interaction each proposal creates (bm x age, kappa x salesprice, tech1 x bm) and on deciles of the model's TRUE conditional SDF weight. Only Proposal 2 mentions this in passing.

CHECK PER-FIRM SIGNAL-TO-NOISE, NOT JUST THE AGGREGATE SHARPE. Several proposals target SR* near 3-4 annualized. That number can be hit two ways: a realistic per-firm cross-sectional R^2 of ~0.5%/month diversified across N = 1000, or an implausible per-firm R^2 diversified less. Proposal 6 explicitly takes the first route (per-stock IR = 0.034) and Proposal 2 the aggregate-factor route; neither reports the resulting cross-sectional predictive R^2 against the real-data benchmark. Report var(rp)/(var(rp) + mean idio var) per month for every calibration and target ~0.005. The current repaired KP14 will be far above it.

ADD AN N-SCALING TABLE FOR ANY PROPOSAL WITH A NEAR-ARBITRAGE COMPONENT. If SR* grows as sqrt(N) (true for Proposal 6 by construction and partly for Proposal 2), the DKKM/FM RATIO must be shown stable across N in {250, 500, 1000, 2000}. If the ratio moves with N you have measured diversification, not complexity. Proposal 6 flags this for itself; it applies to Proposal 2 equally.

CONSIDER PUBLISHING THE NEGATIVE RESULT INSTEAD. The diagnosis phase already establishes something clean, general and novel: under exact K-factor pricing with K small and N large, the population maximum Sharpe is attained to within 0.2% by any well-diversified portfolio with the right factor exposure, so the RFF-over-linear span ratio is 1.00 and NO estimator change can create an advantage. Combined with DKKM's own Theorem 3 (complexity pays iff the eigenvalue spectrum of E[FF'] is flat) and the measured effective rank of ~16 for the configured feature map, that is a precise statement of what standard frictionless production-based models lack. 'Three canonical structural models cannot generate the virtue of complexity, and here is exactly the condition they fail' is a publishable JF-quality paper that requires none of these six changes and cannot be accused of tuning. It is also the framing under which Proposals 1, 3 and 5 become straightforward model corrections rather than suspicious interventions.
